solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thus duck may be seen in Scottish river, indeed!

indicators.note: the pair is seen inside the river, so it sits within it

blocks.note: the Forth, which flows into the Firth of Forth at Edinburgh
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher points out a duck on a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck is not a bird but a cricket score of nothing. The answer is an old exclamation, so the exclamation mark belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic interjection meaning in truth, indeed.

clue.text: French mathematician having love for English design

indicators.note: O (love) is put in place of E (English)

blocks.note: Pierre de Fermat, of the Last Theorem
love = nil in tennis, shaped like O
E = English, the one that goes out

explanation.surface: A French mathematician falls for an English design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having love for English' reads like a romance; it is a swap instruction, O replacing E, turning FERMAT into FORMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a page's format is its layout, the design it follows.

clue.text: Your bar set up for party fun?

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the letters to read from the bottom

blocks.note: yr is the written abbreviation of your
a lever is a bar used to prise

explanation.surface: A barman sets up a bar for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: YR LEVER written upwards reads REVELRY; the surface's party bar is a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively, noisy party enjoyment.

clue.text: Insect moving round on the parrot

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An insect crawls around on a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Orthopterans are the order of grasshoppers, crickets and locusts; the parrot is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orthopteran is any insect of the order Orthoptera, such as a grasshopper.

clue.text: Spot revolutionary protecting a nasty person

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so DOT is turned round
the turned word wraps round A to shield it

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is spotted guarding someone unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel but works as the turning instruction, and 'Spot' reads as a verb when it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad means they are loathsome.

clue.text: A new ship? Very much so!

blocks.note: a dhow is an Arab sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a ship is new and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question and reply look like dialogue; the question is the wordplay and the reply is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'And how!' is an emphatic agreement, just like 'very much so!'.

clue.text: A sort of single person? Not a single person, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the answer is spoken like the word before

blocks.note: not one person is 'none'; say that word and hear how it could be spelt

explanation.surface: A playful riddle about who counts as single.
explanation.walkthrough: A nun is single in the sense of unmarried; the question mark flags that loose sense. NONE and NUN are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is vowed never to marry, so she is a kind of single person.

clue.text: Setter intended to fix locks?

blocks.note: the surface wants the compiler of the crossword; the setter meant is something that sets hair
the surface suggests repairing door locks; the locks are tresses of hair held in place

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, or a locksmith, is meant to mend some locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the compiler of this puzzle and 'locks' the things on doors; here the setter is a styling product and the locks are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gel is a product that sets hair and fixes locks in place.

clue.text: “Sunless” periods, as you might surmise?

blocks.note: reads as dull, overcast spells; Sun is the calendar abbreviation of Sunday, so these are spans with no Sunday in them
the question mark and 'surmise' admit the definition is a playful inference, not a dictionary one

explanation.surface: A gloomy spell of days without sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunless' looks like weather; Sun is the calendar abbreviation of Sunday, and weekdays are the days that exclude it.
explanation.definitionFit: Weekdays are Monday to Friday, the periods without a Sunday.

clue.text: Bolt stand with three legs after first bit has fallen off

indicators.text: after first bit has fallen off
indicators.note: the opening letter is lost

blocks.note: a trivet is a three-legged stand for a pot; drop T

explanation.surface: A three-legged stand loses a piece and is bolted back together.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIVET without its first letter leaves RIVET. 'Bolt' could be a verb for running off, but here it is a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal bolt used to fasten plates together.

clue.text: A row about fellow taking diamonds or another precious stone

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the row is placed around the fellow and his diamonds
a fellow taking something holds it with him, so D is attached to MAN

explanation.surface: An argument about a man who takes diamonds or some other gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is a line of things side by side, and 'or another' tells you the diamonds were only one gem in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Almandine is a deep red garnet, a precious stone other than a diamond.

clue.text: Team is run to develop great players

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new form

explanation.surface: A sports team is being run to develop star players.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting surface points to athletes; the great players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri, the plural of maestro, are distinguished musicians.

clue.text: A period of prosperity in which pound is seen to be blossoming

indicators.note: 'in which' places the pound within the period just named
the pound is seen there, visible inside that period, confirming the placement

blocks.note: A + boom, a time of prosperity

explanation.surface: An economic boom in which sterling thrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound goes into A BOOM: AB(L)OOM. The surface is economics, but 'blossoming' is literal flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tree abloom is in bloom, its flowers open.

clue.text: Act to save time, work unit being made clean

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it inside, so the act holds the rest

blocks.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A time-saving measure makes a work unit clean.
explanation.walkthrough: DEED opens DE…ED to hold T and ERG. Deterge is a rare verb, the root of detergent.
explanation.definitionFit: To deterge is to cleanse, so deterged means made clean.

clue.text: Attractive woman guys without maiden sing about on ship

indicators.note: the guys go without M, dropping it

blocks.note: MEN, less M for maiden (a cricket over with no runs)
SS = steamship, and 'on' puts it after

explanation.surface: Men singing on board a ship about an alluring woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman in the surface; it is the cricket M, taken out of MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchantress is a woman who charms and attracts.

clue.text: A mystical style configured according to a plan

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new configuration

explanation.surface: A mystical design laid out to a precise plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The mystic surface and the orderly answer pull in opposite directions, which helps hide the 14-letter anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something systematically means doing it methodically, according to a plan.

clue.text: Disguising male in the role of ruler

explanation.surface: A man disguises himself to play a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre surface of a man playing a king reads straight through as M + AS + KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting a mask over a face, or a flavour, hides what it really is.

clue.text: Son of Harry maybe watches

definitions.note: 'watches' is a plural noun here, people keeping watch

blocks.note: Potter's, belonging to Harry Potter; 'maybe' flags him as just one Harry

explanation.surface: A son of Prince Harry, perhaps, keeping an eye on things.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry suggests the prince; the needed Harry is Potter, and 'of Harry' makes the possessive Potter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotters are lookouts, people on the watch.

clue.text: Were indecisive priest and actor miscast?

indicators.note: cast wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: A director dithers over whether a priest and actor were wrongly cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a join but is part of the fodder; without it the letters come up three short.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to put off deciding, to be indecisive.

clue.text: Greek avenger, old, remains full of energy

indicators.note: the remains are filled with E

explanation.surface: An aged Greek avenger is still full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes into RESTS before its last letter: RES T(E)S. Orestes avenged his father Agamemnon by killing his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes is the Greek hero who avenged Agamemnon's murder.

clue.text: Impression created by winsome female’s leaving

indicators.note: F goes away from the word

explanation.surface: A charming woman leaves a good impression as she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female's leaving' reads as her departure; it means F leaves FETCHING, which gives ETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print, an impression taken from an etched plate.

clue.text: One of the oppressive types — those people heartlessly rage

indicators.note: with its heart, the middle letters, cut out

blocks.note: THEY, with its middle HE removed

explanation.surface: Oppressors being those people who rage without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' seems to describe the raging, but it applies to THEY, which loses HE.
explanation.definitionFit: By example: despots who crush their subjects are the oppressive types, and any single one of them is a tyrant.

clue.text: Pin never to be inserted the wrong way round in end-piece

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside
the word is turned back to front
names what it goes inside

blocks.note: ne'er, the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: Never fit a pin backwards into the end of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like handyman advice about fitting a pin; 'never' has to become the poetic short form, apostrophe dropped, before it can be turned.
explanation.definitionFit: A treenail is a wooden pin used to fasten timbers.

clue.text: Awkward staff close to mutiny

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word

explanation.surface: Tense staff on the verge of a mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees near revolt; it is a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a sticky moment or wicket is a tricky, awkward one.

clue.text: Founder of religious sect recalled you once entertaining theologian

indicators.note: called back, so the word runs backwards
an entertaining host holds a guest inside

blocks.note: ye, the old form of you

explanation.surface: A cult founder recalls hosting a theologian long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: YE reversed is EY, which holds DD: E(DD)Y. Mary Baker Eddy founded Christian Science.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Baker Eddy founded the Church of Christ, Scientist.

clue.text: Is Parisian classified as “disaffected”?

explanation.surface: Is a Parisian officially labelled a malcontent?
explanation.walkthrough: The Parisian is not a person: 'Is Parisian' asks for the French word for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone estranged from family or party has turned away from it, grown disaffected.

clue.text: Name of murder victim shortened, one way or another!

indicators.note: a word shortened is made shorter at its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis; lose the final L
not wordplay: it flags a second route, via a different murdered man whose first name also shortens

explanation.surface: A murder victim's name is abbreviated in more than one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way or another' says both routes work: ABEL cut short, or Abraham Lincoln, himself murdered, known for short as Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: Abe is a man's name, short for Abraham.

clue.text: Show some incredible vitality

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the last of 'incredible' into the start of 'vitality'

explanation.surface: Put on a display of remarkable energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' reads as a verb; it is the noun, the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón.
explanation.definitionFit: By example: Evita is one particular stage musical, and a musical is a show.

clue.text: Group in home counties — don’t cancel it

blocks.note: the home counties are those around London, in the South East of England
stet, the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand

explanation.surface: A local group is told not to call off its event.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is Latin for 'let it stand', written by an editor to undo a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a group of six, of lines or musicians.

clue.text: Pupil is needed for this crew? Certainly will be in it

indicators.note: the word goes inside the crew

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A school pupil is needed to join this crew, and certainly will be.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupil is not a student but the dark opening in the eye, and a rowing crew is named for its number of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight depends on the pupil letting light into the eye.
